fixes.explanation: Moses it is, friend. The Levite heads say it plainly: "The LORD commanded through Moses that we be given cities in which to live…" (Joshua 21:2). Joshua took over after Moses died (Joshua 1:1). They aren't asking for a favor here. They're pointing to a command that was already given.

Samuel, the prophet (1 Samuel 3:20), is a fair name to think of, friend, but he isn't mentioned anywhere in this passage. Here the Levite heads say the LORD commanded "through Moses" (Joshua 21:2). Moses is the one whose death opens the book of Joshua (Joshua 1:1). Samuel's story comes in 1 Samuel, so save him for there.

Cities to live in. The Levite heads say the LORD commanded "…that we be given cities in which to live…" (Joshua 21:2). Pasturelands for their livestock come along with them. By the end of the passage the count is forty-eight cities (Joshua 21:41). That's a whole lot of front doors, baker.

Tents near the tabernacle is a good guess, because the Levites did camp around it in the wilderness (Numbers 1:53). But that isn't what they ask for here. They say the LORD commanded that they be given "…cities in which to live, together with pasturelands for our livestock." (Joshua 21:2). So the answer is cities, friend, not tents.

That's right, baker. The text says the Israelites gave the Levites these cities and pasturelands "…out of their own inheritance…" (Joshua 21:3). It also says they did it "…by the command of the LORD…" Then the passage moves on to the lots, and the first one comes out for the Kohathite clans (Joshua 21:4).

Joshua 21:3 says the Israelites gave the Levites these cities "…by the command of the LORD…" The verse doesn't mention any waiting. What it does say is that they gave the cities and pasturelands out of their own inheritance. So the answer is that they give, friend, not that they stall.

Most of it sounds humble and reasonable, but the text goes further. It says the LORD gave Israel "…all the land He had sworn to give their fathers…" (Joshua 21:43). That word "all" is right there in the verse. If I ordered a dozen cookies and got eleven, I'd still say the box came up short. Here the box is full.
